results.title: China and India in a standoff at multiple locations along Arunachal border since July, India hosted Xi Jinping from Sep 11-13 for the BRICS
results.description:
China and India in a standoff at multiple locations along Arunachal border since July, India hosted Xi Jinping from Sep 11-13 for the BRICS summit. 
“In the past few-days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues,” ITBP D-G Shatrujeet Kapur said on Thursday.
This is the first official confirmation of the scale of the continuing tensions on the north-eastern border since July this year.
Government sources told The Hindu that since late July, India and China have been engaged in a stand-off at Asaphila near Taksing in Arunachal Pradesh. The Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is said to have pitched tents at an elevation, within 6-7 kilometres of India’s perception of the Line of Actual Control (LAC) near Maja company operating base in Taksing circle of Upper Subansiri district, sources said. results.title: ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur confirmed on October 22 what New Delhi has downplayed for months: Indian and Chinese troops are locke
results.description:
ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur confirmed on October 22 what New Delhi has downplayed for months: Indian and Chinese troops are locked in ongoing face-offs at multiple points in Arunachal Pradesh.

He said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-off happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues.” Kapur called China India’s “biggest adversary.”

The friction began in late July near Maja in Upper Subansiri. Patrols briefly confronted each other and withdrew. Government sources say Chinese troops later returned in larger numbers and pitched tents roughly 6–7 km inside India’s perception of the Line of Actual Control. India reinforced the area. No violence or casualties reported.

India’s Foreign Ministry responded the next day with a familiar line: the border gets “disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces deviate from established patrolling patterns.” Diplomatic and military channels continue.

The face-offs persisted through August boundary talks in Beijing, a first-ever eastern sector Corps Commander meeting on September 6, and the BRICS summit Xi attended in New Delhi. Months of engagement, and troops remain face-to-face.

Kapur used the moment to call for drones, anti-drone systems, underground shelters, and new training to avoid Galwan-style clashes. Opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge called the confirmation “deeply alarming” and demanded the prime minister “come clean.”

Talks and summits have not moved the troops. India’s own border force now says the confrontation continues.

results.title: Chinese troops have pitched tents six to seven kilometers inside what India sees as its border.
results.description:
Chinese troops have pitched tents six to seven kilometers inside what India sees as its border.  🇨🇳🇮🇳

That is according to Indian government sources quoted by The Hindu. The spot is Asaphila, near Taksing, in Arunachal Pradesh. It began in late July, on a routine patrol near Maja. Both sides pulled back. Then, sources say, the Chinese returned in bigger numbers and dug in.
Now India is raising drone platoons and building underground shelters along the line. In 2020 a clash in Galwan killed 20 Indian soldiers. Patrol season in these mountains ends this month. And the tents have not moved.

results.title: Chinese OSINT accounts are circulating selectively edited footage from the July 25, 2026 LAC face-off near Maja in Arunachal Pradesh to push
results.description:
Chinese OSINT accounts are circulating selectively edited footage from the July 25, 2026 LAC face-off near Maja in Arunachal Pradesh to push a narrative of calm border management.
Notice the cropped India Today watermark visible at the 0:11 mark on the left soldier's leg.
The edit keeps a PLA commander speaking in Mandarin about "sincerity" and negotiating a 20-man headcount, followed by PLA troops filming from a ridge while reminding each other to take photos and record video.
What this cut leaves out is the full confrontation: Indian Army and ITBP troops intercepted the PLA patrol inside India's perception of the LAC and forced the initial group to turn back.
Selective video splicing remains a standard tool in modern border information operations. 🇮🇳

results.title: There are mutually agreed disputes sites in Arunachal sector, Asaphila is one of them.
results.description: There are mutually agreed disputes sites in Arunachal sector, Asaphila is one of them. However, this time, the tents have been pitched beyond the agreed disputed sites. And Government never acknowledged the scale of tensions, despite high-level military and diplomatic engagements on the issue. Corps Commander meeting is a first for Arunachal sector, after the 2020 Galwan incident. Any increase in mutually disputed sites eats into India’s territorial claims.

results.title: China doesn't need soldiers to fight the Indian army on the border; they just need a few drone operators who can operate them with precision.
results.description:
China doesn't need soldiers to fight the Indian army on the border; they just need a few drone operators who can operate them with precision. 

< Almost every second Chinese company manufactures drones. 
< They have vast drone technology and production capacity.
< They simply need to pinpoint the exact location of an military post, and they can launch an attack with thousands of drones without using infantry.
< The Chinese are using drone technology for domestic work, logistics, farming, military, and many other things.
